candidates.tagline: NFL team's throwback graphic accidentally looks like a Nazi war flag
candidates.story: On October 21, 2026, the Atlanta Falcons posted a 'throwback weekend' social media graphic showing their 1966 geometric falcon logo centred on vertical red, cream, and gold stripes; 26 million people on X immediately compared it to a World War II-era German military banner, and the internet dubbed it the 'Bird Reich' and '28-3rd Reich.'
candidates.why_funny: The social media team spent time crafting a celebratory throwback graphic and accidentally built a Reichskriegsflagge with a bird on it.
candidates.alt: The Atlanta Falcons 1966 throwback logo — a geometric black-and-cream falcon — centred on bold vertical stripes of red, cream, and gold that drew instant mass comparisons to Nazi-era German war flags when the team posted it on social media in October 2026

candidates.tagline: Apple's $149 'Siri AI speaker' launches Oct 30 — without the Siri AI
candidates.story: Apple announced the HomePod mini 2 at $149 on October 13, 2026, marketing it with 'Siri AI' as the headline upgrade — but the product page footnote reads 'available later in a future software update,' meaning the speaker's entire selling point won't exist when it goes on sale October 30.
candidates.why_funny: Apple named and marketed a product after its AI assistant, put that on the product page, then quietly added a footnote explaining the AI assistant won't actually be in the product at launch.
candidates.alt: Three Apple HomePod mini 2 speakers in green, pink, and blue mesh fabric arranged in a product photograph — Apple's new smart speaker whose flagship Siri AI feature will be absent when it goes on sale October 30, 2026
